messages:
maria: Quick summary from last night's run of the seq-len clustering + kernel probing experiment.
maria: TL;DR — for heavy-tail workloads we see better kernel matches and lower token cost, but probing adds noticeable overhead on short bursts. Need a safe rollout plan.
jin: Can you paste the actual probe/clustering config you used?

maria: Sure — config used in canary:
```
seqcluster:
  enabled: true
  cluster_window_ms: 500
  min_cluster_size: 8
  cluster_similarity_threshold: 0.78
kernel_probe:
  enabled: true
  probe_candidates: ["f16-opt", "int8-qk-fuse", "f16-kcache-opt"]
  probe_budget_per_request: 2
  probe_timeout_ms: 40
  cost_weight: 0.6
```

sam: Nice. What metrics improved vs reg baseline?

maria: Measured over 12h canary (10% traffic). Highlights:
- targeted seq-len group (>1024 tokens): p95 latency -12%, median -7%, tokens/sec +9%
- overall fleet p95 +2% (due to probe tail on many short sessions)
- average cost per 1M tokens: -1.5% on heavy-tail; overall cost +1.1%
- probe failure rate ~0.8% (timeouts or incompatible kernel)

lee: Hmm +2% overall p95 is scary for some apps. Did you try gating probing by request shape?

maria: Yes — we tried two heuristics:
1) skip probing if batch_size * avg_seq_len < 4096
2) only probe when queued latency < 10ms (i.e., not under load)
Result: dropped overall p95 delta from +2% to +0.3%, while keeping most heavy-tail wins.

arnold: We also experimented with an inexpensive prefilter: a fast shape fingerprint that maps seq_len distribution to known-good kernels, then only probe for ambiguous fingerprints.
Example rule (pseudo):
```
if fingerprint in deterministic_map:
  choose deterministic_map[fingerprint]
else:
  allow probing (budget=1)
```
Cut probing budget to 1 reduced probe overhead significantly.

jin: For implementation: we need to expose probing budget and fingerprint map as runtime flags per-pool. Also add telemetry: probe_count, probe_success, probe_latency_hist, chosen_kernel.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for seqcluster-probe-v2 on us-west-2 (10% traffic)

sam: Rollout guard conditions proposal:
- abort if global p95 > baseline_p95 + 5% for 30m
- abort if probe_failure_rate > 3% for 30m
- abort if cost_delta > +3% for 1h
- success if targeted-seqlen p95 improved by >8% for 12h and overall p95 <= +1%

lee: Also add a safety fallback that immediately pins kernel to last-known-good for the customer if we detect jitter > 15% in last 5 mins.

maria: Agreed. Action items:
- jin: add runtime flags + telemetry (priority)
- arnold: build deterministic fingerprint map from 2 weeks of logs and push to config repo
- sam: wire up canary alerts and abort thresholds in deploy playbook
- lee: implement immediate pin fallback (small PR)

maria: One open question — is the fingerprint map a global resource or per-cluster? My vote: per-pool, because hardware mix differs.
jin: per-pool + centralized default fallback. makes sense.

arnold: I'll start extracting fingerprints and put a sample map in repo under infra/kernel-fingerprints.

maria: Cool. If anyone wants to see raw experiment dashboards, ping me — I have the queries and raw traces.

sam: :thumbsup: let's run the 2-week canary with those guards.

lee: :eyes: I'll prioritize the fallback PR today.

maria: Thanks all — we'll reconvene after 48h of canary data.
